result.title: LATCH: LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness for Post-Route FPGA Optimisation
result.summary: Post-route FPGA timing closure remains expert-dependent and computationally expensive. We present LATCH (LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness), a two-layer framework that separates large language model (LLM) orchestration from deterministic FPGA implementation and evaluation. Across sixteen designs and seven LLMs, a single-iteration study compares three agent control granularities - expert-written recipes, direct EDA operations and LLM-constructed procedures - to ask how much control an agent needs per attempt. Functional-pass rates are 98.2%, 71.4% and 17.9%, respectively; yet direct operations give slightly larger 3.4% median Fmax gains when passing, versus 3.2% for recipes. This exposes a trade-off between execution reliability and timing improvement. Informed by this trade-off, a multi-iteration study fixes the action tier at expert recipes to ask how repeated attempts are best organised, comparing a fitted deterministic heuristic with sequential LLM reasoning, branching exploration and knowledge base-guided exploration within 12 checkpoints per run. Branching raises mean maximum-frequency improvement from 10.5% (sequential) to 16.0%, and the knowledge base to 20.3%, improving 15 of 16 designs. Characterisation across 2,421 recipe attempts profiled their gain and validation rates, showing hard-block re-placement gives the largest cumulative mean gain at 41.4MHz.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向 FPGA 布线后时序收敛，提出两层框架 LATCH，把 LLM 编排与确定性的 FPGA 实现评估分离，比较专家配方、直接 EDA 操作与 LLM 自建流程三种代理控制粒度，并在固定动作层级后比较序列推理、分支探索与知识库引导探索等多轮组织方式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其可控性—收益权衡与「序列推理 vs 分支探索 vs 知识库引导」的多轮组织结论，可能为 LVR 迭代推理中的状态更新、搜索式验证与停止决策提供组织线索，可供核查是否迁移；领域为 EDA，与视觉多模态推理无直接联系。
